cells.text: Shots captured divided by shots planned
Under 100 after the shoot day means schedule pickups now
Budget minus the cost of bookings
Negative before post starts means talk to the client about scope
Cuts in client review or revisions
More than two per production means chase and set a firm feedback date
Under seven with open revisions means clear the calendar for the edit

text.text: Most shoot-day problems were decided two weeks earlier. Work this list from the moment the brief is signed.
Two weeks out
Script or interview questions approved in writing
Locations visited; power, parking, sound and light noted
Releases for people and places sent
Crew and gear requests logged in Bookings
One week out
Shot list complete and shared with the director
Call sheet drafted with times, addresses and phone numbers
Weather plan or backup location agreed
Day before
Batteries charged, cards formatted, spares counted
Call sheet sent to every person on the shoot
Client reminded who will be on set and when they arrive
On arrival
Walk the location with the client contact and confirm what is off limits.
Set up audio first; a good picture with bad sound is unusable.
Capture the hardest shots while the light and the people are fresh.
During the day
Tick off shots in the Shot list as they are captured, and mark misses Pickup needed straight away.
Slate or name each take so the editor can find it.
Back up every card before it is formatted, to two places.
At wrap
All releases signed
Cards labelled and backed up twice
Gear counted back into cases
Client told what happens next and when they will see a cut
The rounds

cells.text: Rough cut, no color or final music

text.text: Collecting feedback
Send one link with a feedback due date.
Ask for one consolidated list from one person.
Log notes in the Cut row with timecodes.
Limits
Two rounds of changes are included; extra rounds are quoted before work starts.
Changes to the story after the fine cut count as a new edit.
Delivery
Export the agreed formats, name files clearly, send the checksum list and move the production to Delivered with Close out.
What to ask first
Where will it run: social, a website, an event screen, television?
How long should it be, and how many versions?
Who is on screen, and do they need to be booked?
Building the number
List crew days, gear days, locations, talent and post days as lines in Bookings.
Add a buffer of ten to fifteen percent for pickups and extra rounds.
Compare Crew and gear costs against the budget on the production row and note the margin.
Terms to state
Number of included revisions.
Usage rights and music licensing.
Cancellation and weather days.
What the client must supply and by when.
